21 The diagram shows a transverse wave on a rope. The wave is travelling from left to right.
At the instant shown, the points P and Q on the rope have zero displacement and maximum
displacement respectively.

Which row describes the direction of motion, if any, of the points P and Q at this instant?

hints: Notice where P and Q sit on the shape: P is on the rising slope crossing the equilibrium line just left of a crest, Q is exactly on the crest, and the whole shape is travelling from left to right.
Imagine the whole sine shape shifted a tiny distance to the right: the rope height that was just to the left of each point will arrive at that point next.
Apply that shift to P where lower rope from toward the trough arrives next, and recall that a particle at maximum displacement in transverse oscillation momentarily stops before reversing.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: transverse wave on a rope moving left to right, P at zero displacement on the slope up to the crest Q, Q at maximum positive displacement.
State the physical rule: rope particles move only up and down, and their next displacement is the displacement of the profile just to the left when the wave moves right.
Consider point P: just to its left the rope is lower, down toward the trough, so as the profile shifts right that lower height arrives at P.
Therefore P must move downwards at this instant, with large speed because zero-displacement points have maximum transverse speed.
Consider point Q: it is at the crest, the maximum displacement, so in its up-down oscillation it momentarily stops before moving back down.
Therefore Q is stationary at this instant, giving P downwards and Q stationary. This is option A.

A.explanation: P is on the upward slope just left of the crest and the profile moving right brings lower rope to P, so P moves downwards, while Q at the crest is at maximum displacement with instantaneously zero velocity.

B.explanation: P is not stationary because a zero-displacement point on a moving slope has maximum particle speed, and Q is not moving downwards at the instant of maximum displacement.

C.explanation: P is not stationary for a travelling wave, and Q cannot be moving upwards because it is already at the top crest and must next move down or stop instantaneously.

D.explanation: P does not move upwards because the trough to its left is moving right toward P, pulling P down, although Q being stationary is correct.
